envelope.name: id
envelope.doc: event id (nanoid). primary key — re-posting a batch after a flaky flush is idempotent, never a double count.

envelope.name: at
envelope.doc: ms since epoch, stamped by the PRODUCER. client clocks can skew; ingest keeps them honest by clamping absurd values (see db.ts).

envelope.name: kind
envelope.doc: event kind — a key of EVENTS.

envelope.name: device
envelope.doc: stable per-device id from localStorage, or the literal 'server' for events the brain emits.

envelope.name: device_class
envelope.doc: coarse device family: derived from the ua at registration, or claimed explicitly by a ua-less client (the board daemon): ipad | iphone | mac | android | desktop | board | server.

envelope.name: surface
envelope.doc: which screen the event happened on: home | thread | compose | machines | settings | history | day | review | term | login. null for server events. term is the terminal pane wherever it is placed (visor, deck, room) — a need served while the visor is up still counts on its underlying surface, so term only stamps events the pane itself fires.

envelope.name: host
envelope.doc: fleet machine id, the host name from boxbox.toml (e.g. desk, vm).

envelope.name: session
envelope.doc: session key, `${host}:${sessionID}` — the same identity the client uses everywhere.

envelope.name: ok
envelope.doc: 1 succeeded, 0 failed, null not applicable. every outcome-bearing event sets it, which makes failure rate a one-line query.

envelope.name: ms
envelope.doc: duration in ms where the event has one (verb round trip, surface paint, need latency). null otherwise.

envelope.name: props
envelope.doc: json bag of the kind-specific props. never query this directly — use the generated per-kind view, which flattens it into real columns.

events.doc: a client booted the store. the entry prop is the honest answer to 'what pulled him in' — a push tap is a very different session from a deliberate cold open.

props.name: entry
props.doc: what brought him here

props.name: standalone
props.doc: 1 = installed pwa (home screen), 0 = browser tab. the ipad story depends on which of these he actually uses.

props.name: ua
props.doc: raw user agent, kept once per open for device forensics.

props.name: viewport
props.doc: `${width}x${height}` css px at boot.

props.name: offlineSpool
props.doc: events recovered from the localStorage spool at boot — nonzero means the last visit ended with an unflushed tail (backgrounded, killed, or offline).

events.doc: the tab became visible. paired with app.hidden this is the ground truth for attention time, and it is what v_stints sessionizes.

props.name: awayMs
props.doc: how long it was hidden before this.

events.doc: the tab went away (pocketed, app-switched, locked). the emitter flushes its queue on this transition via sendBeacon.

props.name: visibleMs
props.doc: how long it was visible before this.

events.doc: the multiplexed sse connection changed state. reconnect churn per device class is the quiet tax nobody has ever measured — ios backgrounding is the suspect.

props.name: state
props.doc: connection transition

props.name: downMs
props.doc: how long the stream was down before a reopen.

props.name: resumed
props.doc: 1 = the connection resumed from the device's cursor and the server replayed the gap, 0 = it started over from a reset and a snapshot. v2: every reconnect should be a 1.

props.name: replayed
props.doc: journal entries the server replayed from the cursor before the stream was live again. v2.

events.doc: a screen was opened. the surface column carries which one. coverage across a month answers which surfaces are dead weight (see the kill list in docs/migration-v2.md) without guessing.

props.name: from
props.doc: the surface he came from.

props.name: route
props.doc: the concrete path, e.g. /t/desk:ses_abc.

events.doc: the surface painted something meaningful (transcript rows present, not a spinner). ms carries the wait. over tailscale on a tablet this is a real story.

props.name: cached
props.doc: 1 = served from the client cache, 0 = waited on the wire.

events.doc: a send from the composer, timed from the tap to the journal entry carrying its clientID: the daemon's echo, never the local call (for a shell line, whose output is its echo, the daemon's answer). ok = 1 when the echo arrived, 0 when the send failed or the echo never came within 30 s of live stream; ms is tap to echo, retries and time offline included. the budget is p90 under 400 ms.

props.name: verb
props.doc: what was sent: a prompt that started a turn, one queued behind it, a steer, an answer to an ask, a `!` line, a `/` command, or the first prompt of a new thread

props.name: retries
props.doc: how many times the same clientID was posted again after a timeout before the echo (a4: never a double).

props.name: queued
props.doc: 1 = the daemon held it behind a running turn as a provisional message, 0 = it started a turn or went straight in.

props.name: chars
props.doc: length of what was sent. never the text.

props.name: photos
props.doc: photos on the message, clamped on the device.

events.doc: the app asked the server for a repo's favicon, one row per read (docs/design.md, the repo mark; a repo is read again only when its last answer falls due). outcome is what the server said: an image, or why there is none (none, unsupported while the daemon has no file-read route, unproven while the host has not shown the root to be real, refused for the host user's home or a directory above it), or nothing usable (retry: dropped, timed out, a server error, the lookup not finished; unreadable: bytes that are not a drawable image). ms is the fetch and the read of the pixels; ok = 1 for an image, 0 for retry or unreadable, absent for a clean answer of no icon. no host or repo name travels. a long ms with retry is the daemon's file lookups queueing behind each other.

props.name: outcome
props.doc: what came of the read

props.name: attempts
props.doc: the repo's consecutive retries including this one, 0 when the read was not a retry.

events.doc: the server rebuilt the board's view (docs/board.md, cost) and sent it: one row a minute at most while a board stream listens, none without one. ms is the rebuild and encode, rounded; us the same in microseconds, since the budget is under 1 ms. no thread, host or machine name travels.

props.name: us
props.doc: the rebuild and encode, in microseconds.

props.name: bytes
props.doc: the encoded view frame's size.

props.name: threads
props.doc: threads riding the view, at most 36.

events.doc: the thread's paints, an intent to the first frame that shows its result: a thread opening, a row opening, a stream event reaching a glyph. ms is intent to paint; ok = 1 when it painted inside its budget (a thread from cache in 300 ms, a row in one frame, an event in 150 ms).

props.name: what
props.doc: which budget

props.name: cached
props.doc: 1 = painted from the client cache, 0 = waited on the wire.

props.name: messages
props.doc: messages in the thread when it painted (thread only).

events.doc: what the sync worker did with its indexeddb cache (docs/architecture.md, indexeddb layout), one row per event. boot: the launch read the meta, the fleet and every thread's head and the pages of the thread the url opens, nothing else; ms is that read, threads the cached threads known, messages the ones read. restore: a thread opened or held was read back from its pages before the wire was asked; ms is the read, ok = 0 when a page was missing and the thread starts over from the daemon. evict: a thread left the cache for the thread cap (40) or the byte cap (50 mb), held-only threads first; opened says the person had it open, and a 1 should be rare, and cap says which limit did it.

props.name: what
props.doc: which event

props.name: threads
props.doc: boot: threads cached; restore and evict: 1.

props.name: messages
props.doc: messages read from the cache (boot: those of the url's thread).

props.name: bytes
props.doc: the thread's size by the cap's estimate (the size of its json), for restore and evict.

props.name: opened
props.doc: evict only: 1 = the person had opened the thread, 0 = it was held for another thread.

props.name: cap
props.doc: evict only: the limit that evicted it. opened = the person's 40 threads, held = a released place of the 16 for held threads, taken by a new hold, bytes = the 50 mb cap, unfit = a held thread's read (or its growth) that could not fit beside the thread on stage and the other leased threads, so nothing else was evicted for it.

events.doc: what the sync worker's stream connection cost it, in counts and sizes, never content (docs/architecture.md, the sync worker). minute: one row a minute while the stream is up, and one for the part of a minute when it closes; ms is the window, and an idle fleet should cost little in it. overflow: a frame passed the parser's cap (32 mb of text, four times the largest the server forwards), so the connection was dropped and resumed from its cursor; a well-formed stream never sends one.

props.name: what
props.doc: which row

props.name: view
props.doc: minute: what the page showed when the row was written (docs/protocol.md, interest): home = no thread on stage, the overview only; thread = a thread on stage, with its words; hidden = hidden for 30 s, the overview only.

props.name: frames
props.doc: minute: sse frames received (journal, colour and board frames).

props.name: received
props.doc: minute: bytes read off the stream. overflow: the characters the parser held at the cap.

props.name: skipped
props.doc: minute: journal seqs the stream skipped, from the ids it showed: the transcript entries of threads outside the page's interest, which protocol 3 never sends it. a home page skips most of the journal; a skipped seq is never a gap.

props.name: posts
props.doc: minute: patch messages posted to the ui thread (one a frame at most).

props.name: patches
props.doc: minute: patches in them, after coalescing.

props.name: posted
props.doc: minute: about how many bytes those patches carried (strings by length, 8 a number).

props.name: saves
props.doc: minute: indexeddb saves committed (one in flight at most).

props.name: puts
props.doc: minute: indexeddb records those saves put.

props.name: stored
props.doc: minute: about how many bytes those records held, by the same estimate as posted.

events.doc: how a stream connection of the sync worker opened (docs/protocol.md, catch-up), one row per connection that reached its catch-up's end. caught = the server caught the device's cursor up (overview changes, then each interest thread's transcript from its left) and said caught; reset = it could not (no cursor, another epoch, expired, invalid) and sent the whole fleet, and the threads on screen are read again. ms (in the envelope) is the dial to the caught or the reset applied.

props.name: how
props.doc: how it ended

props.name: reason
props.doc: reset only: the reset's reason.

props.name: frames
props.doc: frames after the hello up to and including the caught or the reset.

props.name: bytes
props.doc: the characters of those frames' data, as they arrived (inflated).

props.name: stale
props.doc: thread.stale frames: interest threads whose missed entries the server no longer held, read before they are trusted.

props.name: resets
props.doc: thread.reset frames: threads the server could not vouch for, whose messages were dropped and read again.

events.doc: the server confirmed what the page shows (docs/protocol.md, the confirm), one row per confirm of the newest interest post: a thread opened, closed or held, or the page hidden for 30 s or shown again. ms (in the envelope) is the post to the confirm; the switch shows no gap whatever it is, and a long one is a slow stream.

props.name: entering
props.doc: threads that entered the interest at this confirm.

props.name: catchup
props.doc: the characters of the catch-up frames that came ahead of the confirm (entering threads' transcripts from their left).

props.name: stale
props.doc: entering threads the server could not catch up, read instead.

props.name: reset
props.doc: entering threads the server had reset since their left, dropped and read again.

events.doc: a protocol 3 rule caught something on the device (docs/protocol.md, tests), one row per event. patch-error: a thread or order patch that did not fit what the device held, so nothing of it applied and the stream reconnected with a reset; catchup-error: a catch-up or confirm frame that did not parse, handled the same way; read-late: a thread read that started before the thread entered the interest, taken again; hash-miss: a settled part whose text the device did not hold exactly (textOf), so its message was read again. a well-behaved server and network cause none of the first two.

props.name: what
props.doc: which rule

events.doc: media paints and serves (docs/design.md, voice and media; docs/agents.md, media). card and viewer are the app's: an image card's image painted within 300 ms of entering the view, the viewer opened within its spring; ok = 1 inside the budget. serve is the server's: GET /api/media/{id} from the request to the answer's head (the index read, the file opened), one row per play or open (a whole file, a range from byte 0, or a refusal), never one per scrub; ok = 1 when the file was served (200, 206, 304), 0 for a refusal (400, 404, 410, 416, 503).

props.name: what
props.doc: which paint or serve

props.name: status
props.doc: serve only: the http status answered.

props.name: bytes
props.doc: serve: the bytes the answer carries (the range's length for a 206); card and viewer: the image's size.

events.doc: a file reached the media store, or was refused: one row per upload (POST /api/media) or agent copy (the ingest the sources call on first sight). ms is the whole take, the body streamed, hashed and committed; ok = 1 when the store holds the bytes (stored or duplicate). a run of busy uploads says four were in flight; full says nothing old enough was left to evict and [media] max_bytes wants raising.

props.name: origin
props.doc: who brought the bytes

props.name: outcome
props.doc: stored: new bytes written. duplicate: the store held them already (an upload retried, a voice note read back from the agent). busy: four uploads (or eight copies) were running. too-large: past 64 MiB. empty: no bytes. refused-kind: a declared image, audio or video type the bytes contradict (uploads only). full: no room even after evicting everything allowed to go. source-failed: the body stopped arriving. failed: the disk or the store failed.

props.name: family
props.doc: the declared type's family, never the type or a name

props.name: bytes
props.doc: the file's size when it was read whole, else the length its sender announced; null when neither is known.

events.doc: the media store dropped its least recently used files to make room for a new one (docs/agents.md, media, eviction): one row per eviction, which runs until the store, the new file included, is under 90% of the cap. pinned files and files under a day old never go. their ids answer 410 from then on.

props.name: files
props.doc: how many files went.

props.name: bytes
props.doc: the bytes they freed.

props.name: total
props.doc: the bytes the store holds after, the new file included.

props.name: cap
props.doc: [media] max_bytes.

events.doc: what the thread's memo caches held when a thread's stage closed (docs/thread.md, what is remembered): one row for each cache. the turns the stage built, the row models of settled turns, the sanitised html of settled markdown, and the heights of turns that were measured. bytes is what the cache alone keeps alive against its cap, hits and misses count its reads over its life, evicted the entries its cap pushed out.

props.name: what
props.doc: which cache

props.name: entries
props.doc: entries held.

props.name: bytes
props.doc: what they cost, by the cache's estimate.

props.name: hits
props.doc: reads that found their entry, since the app started.

props.name: misses
props.doc: reads that did not.

props.name: evicted
props.doc: entries the byte cap pushed out.

events.doc: one AppActions call: the complete record of what he asked boxbox to do. ok + ms come from the call's own outcome, so per-verb failure rate and latency need no extra instrumentation.

props.name: name
props.doc: the AppActions method name, verbatim.

props.name: arg
props.doc: the one argument worth keeping for this verb, per the redaction allowlist in instrument.ts (a reply choice, a machine id, a workspace mode), or the verb's own outcome where that is the story (flushQueued: fire | arm | ignore, the box box gate's decision). never free text.

props.name: chars
props.doc: length of any text argument. the text itself never travels.

props.name: files
props.doc: attached file count where the verb takes files.

props.name: error
props.doc: failure message when ok = 0.

events.doc: a session started needing him. permission, question and fault are raised SERVER-side off the frames, so the clock does not depend on any client being awake. unread and review are client-derived (they need read state and checkout state), so the first client to see one raises it and the server dedupes by session+need until it clears — N open tabs still produce one raise.

props.name: need
props.doc: which kind

props.name: child
props.doc: 1 = a subagent raised it.

props.name: id
props.doc: v2: the need's id (`ask:<host>:<id>`, `done:<host>:<session>:<message>`), the join key to need.served and to the push notice of the same id.

events.doc: a need first rendered on a client's screen. raised → seen measures delivery (push, stream, his pocket); seen → served measures the ui. v_needs pairs a sighting to its raise by time and session, never by a shared stamp — the two sides are stamped by different clocks.

props.name: need
props.doc: which kind

events.doc: the need went away. by = him when a verb of his cleared it, agent when the loop moved on by itself, expired when it aged out unanswered. the agent/expired share is the honest count of needs boxbox raised and he never served.

props.name: need
props.doc: which kind

props.name: by
props.doc: who cleared it. the SERVER always fills this — the need tracker owns the attribution because only it knows when the raise happened and whether serving evidence landed. a client emitting this kind is sending a signal, not a record: the route hands it to the tracker and never stores the client's row.

props.name: ageMs
props.doc: how long it stood.

events.doc: v2: a person served a need: answered it, looked at it, carried the thread on. the server writes it, from the fleet's own derivation (docs/architecture.md: computed once), with ms the time it stood since need.raised. needs that went away without a person are need.cleared with by = agent or expired. v2 raises done where v1 raised unread, and never raises one he watched settle.

props.name: need
props.doc: which kind

props.name: by
props.doc: the device id that served it, or the daemon's name for another client that did.

props.name: how
props.doc: answered: an ask got its answer. seen: the thread was on stage on a looking device, or marked read. continued: a new turn started there.

props.name: id
props.doc: the need's id, the join key to need.raised and push.acted.

events.doc: v2: the server judged a notice, the suppressed ones included, so a dead funnel shows in a day, not months later. one row per notice; the pushes it caused are push.sent rows with the same id.

props.name: reason
props.doc: why it did or did not go out. sent: to at least one device. watched: a device was looking at the thread (visible and focused within 90 s). continued: a waiting done was dropped because the agent carried on. not-armed: a done for a turn nobody started. own-action, subagent, replayed: never pushed. no-subscriptions: no device is subscribed. kind-off: no device wants this kind. duplicate: every device already had this notice.

props.name: need
props.doc: what it was about: question | permission | done | fault | ready.

props.name: tag
props.doc: the thread tag, `thread:${host}:${session}`: the join key to push.sent and push.tapped.

props.name: devices
props.doc: how many devices it was queued for; 0 unless sent.

props.name: id
props.doc: the notice id (`ask:<id>`, `done:<message id>`), stable per event: the join key to push.sent, push.delivered and push.tapped.

events.doc: the server sent a web push. joined to push.tapped this is the delivery funnel: sent → tapped → acted, per need kind. v2 writes one row per device, with ok from the push service's answer (201), never from having tried, and ms the time to that answer across retries.

props.name: need
props.doc: what it was about.

props.name: tag
props.doc: dedupe tag, the join key to a tap.

props.name: subs
props.doc: how many subscriptions it fanned out to (v2: always 1, one row per device).

props.name: target
props.doc: v2: the device id it was sent to, the same id that device stamps on its own rows.

props.name: status
props.doc: v2: the push service's http status; null when it was never reached.

props.name: attempts
props.doc: v2: posts made, retries included (at most 3).

props.name: id
props.doc: v2: the notice id, the join key to push.decided and push.delivered.

events.doc: v2: the device's service worker received the push and showed its notification, with or without the app open. sent → delivered is the push service's leg; delivered → tapped is the person's.

props.name: need
props.doc: what it was about.

props.name: tag
props.doc: the thread tag.

props.name: id
props.doc: the notice id.

props.name: open
props.doc: 1 = an app window was open when it arrived (hidden or not), 0 = the app was closed.

events.doc: a banner was tapped open. the gap to push.sent is how long the pocket took.

props.name: tag
props.doc: the tag of the push that was tapped.

props.name: action
props.doc: v2: which part was tapped: answer | open (the action buttons chromium shows), or banner (the notification itself, the only choice on ios).

props.name: need
props.doc: v2: what it was about.

props.name: id
props.doc: v2: the notice id.

props.name: open
props.doc: v2: 1 = an existing app window was focused, 0 = the tap launched the app.

events.doc: v2: a need that was pushed was then served by a person, from any device. the last step of the funnel: decided → sent → delivered → tapped → acted. ms is the time from the push going out to the need served; the server writes it, joined by the notice id.

props.name: need
props.doc: what it was about: question | permission | done | fault | ready.

props.name: tag
props.doc: the thread tag.

props.name: id
props.doc: the notice id.

props.name: by
props.doc: the device id that served it, or the daemon's name for another client.

props.name: how
props.doc: how it was served: answered | seen | continued | settled.

events.doc: he answered straight from the banner without opening the app — the fastest possible path, and worth knowing how often it actually works.

props.name: need
props.doc: permission | question.

props.name: tag
props.doc: the tag of the push that was answered — the join key back to push.sent, same as a tap.

props.name: action
props.doc: the action id the banner fired.

events.doc: the same control fired three or more times inside a second, or fired and nothing changed. the app was not listening, or looked like it wasn't.

props.name: control
props.doc: accessible name of the control.

props.name: taps
props.doc: how many times.

props.name: inert
props.doc: 1 = no state change followed the tap at all.

events.doc: he opened a surface and bounced straight back out (<2s). either it was the wrong door or it had nothing for him.

props.name: to
props.doc: the surface he bounced off.

props.name: backMs
props.doc: how long he lasted.

events.doc: something was typed and thrown away. an abandoned compose is a thought boxbox failed to make cheap enough to finish.

props.name: what
props.doc: what was abandoned

props.name: chars
props.doc: how much had been typed.

props.name: files
props.doc: attachments staged and dropped.

props.name: heldMs
props.doc: how long it was open.

events.doc: keyboard-adjacent viewport geometry worth a row. fix=release: webkit claimed a keyboard-sized overlap with nothing editable focused and KeyboardWatch forcibly released the shrunk shell (once per episode). fix=snapshot: the settled geometry vector after EVERY keyboard close — the affidavit that catches lies BELOW the overlap math (stale layout viewport, stale safe-area inset, compositor desync), filed because the 2026-07-25 stuck gap showed zero release rows while plainly visible. screenH is the device truth no viewport lie touches; compare everything against it.

props.name: fix
props.doc: what this row is

props.name: overlap
props.doc: clientHeight - visualViewport.height, css px.

props.name: offsetTop
props.doc: visualViewport.offsetTop.

props.name: vvHeight
props.doc: visualViewport.height.

props.name: clientHeight
props.doc: documentElement.clientHeight — the layout viewport / what 100dvh keys off.

props.name: sabPx
props.doc: measured px of --sab (env safe-area-inset-bottom, css-capped at 40px) via a probe element.

props.name: frameBottom
props.doc: getBoundingClientRect().bottom of [data-bb-frame] — where the shell actually ends in viewport coords.

props.name: screenH
props.doc: screen.height — device truth, immune to every viewport lie.

events.doc: an unhandled rejection or a failed fetch on a client. tagged with the verb in flight so errors point at intent, not at a stack frame.

props.name: message
props.doc: the error message, truncated.

props.name: verb
props.doc: the AppActions call in flight, if any.

props.name: status
props.doc: http status where there was one.

events.doc: he sent work to an agent. the powertrain is captured AS DRIVEN — the overrides that actually rode the wire, not the defaults.

props.name: model
props.doc: modelID as sent.

props.name: provider
props.doc: providerID as sent.

props.name: agent
props.doc: agent type as sent (build, plan, a subagent name).

props.name: variant
props.doc: reasoning variant as sent.

props.name: workspace
props.doc: where it runs

props.name: fresh
props.doc: 1 = this prompt created the session.

props.name: chars
props.doc: prompt length. the prompt itself never travels.

props.name: files
props.doc: attachments.

props.name: queued
props.doc: 1 = the loop was busy and the serve queued it.

events.doc: one settled assistant message, with its model and its bill. emitted server-side off the same frames the spend ledger counts, deduped by message id. ms carries the turn duration.

props.name: model
props.doc: modelID that billed.

props.name: provider
props.doc: providerID that billed.

props.name: usd
props.doc: cost of this message.

props.name: msg
props.doc: message id — the dedupe key.

props.name: tokensIn
props.doc: input tokens.

props.name: tokensOut
props.doc: output tokens.

props.name: tokensReasoning
props.doc: reasoning tokens.

props.name: cacheRead
props.doc: cache read tokens.

props.name: cacheWrite
props.doc: cache write tokens.

events.doc: a thread (or everything) was marked read, and on which device. the whole reason this exists: read state used to be device-local, so a fresh ipad showed a hundred phantom unreads.

props.name: scope
props.doc: one thread or the lot

props.name: source
props.doc: what marked it

props.name: device
props.doc: v2: the device whose mark moved (the server writes read.mark; watched = on stage on a looking device).

props.name: count
props.doc: threads cleared when scope = all.

props.name: staleMs
props.doc: how long the thread had been unread before he got to it.

events.doc: v2: threads were cleared off home, from one window or with 'clear done'. ok is 1 when every thread asked for was cleared; refused counts the ones that were not (still working, waiting on an answer, a subagent, not in the fleet). a cleared thread comes back on its own when it works, asks or is updated, and stays in history: the share that comes back inside a minute says whether people clear what they still want.

props.name: source
props.doc: the control: window (one window's clear) or done (the bar's 'clear done').

props.name: count
props.doc: threads cleared.

props.name: refused
props.doc: threads asked for and not cleared.

events.doc: v2: a thread was archived from its menu. ok is the daemon's answer (cmx2's PATCH with time.archived), never the tap: null when the daemon took the patch and did not answer in time, or answered past reading (it may be archived).

v2: a thread was renamed from its menu. ok is the daemon's answer (cmx2's PATCH with title), never the tap: null when the daemon took the patch and did not answer in time. the title is never recorded.

v2: a thread was forked, from its menu (the whole thread) or from a turn (cut before the next turn's prompt), through the server's fork verb (cmx2's POST /session/:id/fork). ok is the agent's answer, never the tap: 1 for the new thread, 0 for a refusal or an agent not reached, null when the agent took the fork and its answer was lost (no answer in time, or one that could not be read: the fork may exist). cut says what it held, outcome how it went; no title, message or id is recorded.

props.name: cut
props.doc: what the fork holds: the whole thread, or the thread through one turn.

props.name: outcome
props.doc: how it went: done, refused (the agent said no: a turn or thread gone, browse-only history, no fork), failed (the agent was not reached or was busy) or unknown (taken, answer lost).

events.doc: v2: a side question was asked about a thread from the composer's btw mode (cmx2's POST /session/:id/btw, through the server). ok is the daemon's answer, never the tap. outcome: done (the daemon took it; the answer streams after), gone (no such thread), refused (the daemon said no, or the question was not one), unsupported (the agent or its daemon has no btw) or failed (the host did not answer). chars is the question's length; the question is never recorded.

props.name: outcome
props.doc: how the ask went.

props.name: chars
props.doc: length of the question in characters.

events.doc: v2: a btw card was dismissed, on every device (cmx2's POST /session/:id/btw/:btw/dismiss, through the server). ok is the daemon's answer, never the tap. outcome as btw.asked, gone meaning the btw no longer exists.

props.name: outcome
props.doc: how the dismissal went.

events.doc: v2: a btw's question and answer were added to its thread as a user message, a steer while a turn ran or a prompt otherwise (cmx2's POST /session/:id/btw/:btw/promote, through the server). ok is the daemon's answer, never the tap. outcome as btw.asked; refused is a btw still running or added already.

props.name: outcome
props.doc: how the promotion went.

events.doc: v2: a checkout's branch was squash-merged into its base from the review card (cmx2's /experimental/worktree/merge, through the server). ok is the daemon's answer, never the tap. outcome says how it went: done, busy (a turn runs in the checkout), conflict (the branch conflicts with its base), refused (dirty, nothing to merge, detached, or the base is dirty), gone (the checkout was merged or discarded already) or failed (the host did not answer). no path, message or file name is recorded.

props.name: outcome
props.doc: how the merge went.

events.doc: v2: a checkout and its branch were removed without merging, from the review card (cmx2's /experimental/worktree/discard, through the server). ok is the daemon's answer, never the tap. outcome says how it went: done, busy (a turn runs in the checkout), gone (the checkout was merged or discarded already) or failed.

props.name: outcome
props.doc: how the discard went.

events.doc: v2: one page of history was read through the server (every host's threads, newest first, past home's 12 hours). rows is what came back, hosts how many machines were asked, unreached how many did not answer, chars the length of the search (never the text), ms the time to the merged answer. a search that scans a long way shows as ms.

props.name: rows
props.doc: threads in the page.

props.name: hosts
props.doc: machines asked.

props.name: unreached
props.doc: machines that did not answer.

props.name: chars
props.doc: length of the search; 0 when there was none.

props.name: paged
props.doc: 1 when the page continued an earlier one (a 'before' cursor), 0 for the first.

events.doc: a session compacted on some host. the client learns it from the serve's session.compacted frame, so it counts folds it WATCHED — a fold that happened with no client awake is not in here. how often threads hit the wall, how much context the fold gives back, and how long he waits for it are all unmeasured today; auto vs manual says whether he ever gets ahead of it.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: who called the stop: auto is the serve on its own threshold, manual is his compact verb.

props.name: overflow
props.doc: 1 = the fold also stripped media to fit the byte cap.

props.name: tokensBefore
props.doc: context tokens the serve counted before folding.

props.name: durationMs
props.doc: how long the fold took.

props.name: summaryChars
props.doc: length of the summary the fold wrote. the summary text never travels.

events.doc: a cold launch painted its first real screen. ms is from navigation start to the first frame that showed it. a page opened behind another, or hidden before it painted, reports none. target p50 300 ms, p90 700 ms from cache.

props.name: cached
props.doc: 1 = the screen was painted from the device cache before the stream answered, 0 = it waited on the stream.

props.name: windows
props.doc: windows on that first screen.

events.doc: tap to first frame of the response: ms from the input event to the end of the first frame that rendered what it opened (style, layout and paint done). target 1 frame.

props.name: control
props.doc: what was tapped: a window, the capsule, back, or a window's answer pill (option was a window's own option button, which no longer exists)

props.name: arrangement
props.doc: the layout at the time

props.name: frames
props.doc: animation frames between the input and that paint; 1 is the budget.

events.doc: input to paint for one interaction, from the browser's event timing: ms from the input to the next paint after its handlers ran. the page's first input is always reported; after it, only interactions over 16 ms are.

props.name: type
props.doc: the event type (pointerup, click, keydown)

events.doc: layout shift over one visible stretch, reported when the page hides. the budget is 0.

props.name: score
props.doc: cumulative layout shift, in thousandths.

props.name: shifts
props.doc: layout-shift entries not caused by recent input.

events.doc: a task on the ui thread over 50 ms. ms is its duration. the budget is none during streaming or scrolling.

props.name: during
props.doc: what the ui was doing

events.doc: one transition's frames: ms is its measured duration. the budget is no dropped frame at 60 fps.

props.name: transition
props.doc: which motion

props.name: frames
props.doc: frames painted during it.

props.name: dropped
props.doc: frame gaps over 1.5 times the display's frame time.

events.doc: a browser attached to a terminal through the relay. ok = 1 once cmx2's end-of-replay frame arrived (the pane is showing the terminal), 0 when the relay could not reach it; ms is the upgrade to that frame.

props.name: resume
props.doc: 1 = the browser passed its cursor (it lost its socket and came back), 0 = an open that replays everything cmx2 retained.

props.name: replayed
props.doc: output cmx2 replayed before going live, in utf-16 units.

props.name: dropped
props.doc: output between the cursor and the replay that cmx2 no longer held, in utf-16 units. nonzero means the pane reset and painted the tail.

props.name: error
props.doc: why the relay could not reach the terminal when ok = 0, in plain words.

events.doc: the relay lost cmx2 and redialled it with its cursor, keeping the browser's socket open. ok = 1 once the redial's end-of-replay frame arrived; ms is from losing cmx2 to that frame.

props.name: cause
props.doc: why the relay let go of cmx2: the connection dropped, it went 45 s without a byte, or live output found the queue to the browser full.

props.name: replayed
props.doc: output the redial replayed, in utf-16 units.

props.name: dropped
props.doc: output cmx2 no longer held by the time the relay came back, in utf-16 units.

props.name: error
props.doc: why the redial failed when ok = 0, in plain words.

events.doc: a relay's traffic, once, when it ends. ms is how long it lived. the pair with term.open says how terminals are used: opened and read, or typed into.

props.name: down
props.doc: output bytes sent to the browser, replays included.

props.name: up
props.doc: input bytes the browser typed into the terminal.

props.name: redials
props.doc: times the relay redialled cmx2 (term.reconnect rows).

props.name: overflows
props.doc: times live output found the 256 kb queue to the browser full.

props.name: end
props.doc: why the relay ended: the browser left, the shell exited, the host forgot the terminal, the host stopped answering, the browser went 45 s silent, it typed faster than the terminal read, the server stopped, or the host refused the credential.

events.doc: the daemon attached to the board: HELLO round trip done, palette pushed, render loop starting. reconnect churn is the health signal — a recurring watchdog trip shows up here as reconnects climbing.

props.name: fw
props.doc: firmware version from the 0x81 HELLO reply.

props.name: proto
props.doc: protocol version from the HELLO reply.

props.name: reconnects
props.doc: reattach count for this daemon process before this one. 0 on first light.

events.doc: one physical keypress, as the daemon derived it. ok + ms ride the envelope from the resulting call's own outcome. this kind is invisible to v_needs by design — a press that serves a need emits a generic `verb` row alongside.

props.name: wire
props.doc: wire index 0-16, the daemon + /board sim ordering (never the led or matrix order).

props.name: verb
props.doc: the derived verb, from the locked four-verb grammar

props.name: target
props.doc: what the key pointed at — a kind (seat, machine, need, mode, radio), never content.

props.name: bank
props.doc: which bank the board was in

events.doc: a livery binding changed: an agent bound to a key, or cleared from one. rare and deliberate. bet 4 (bound keys beat the omni-switcher to a thread) is checked against these.

props.name: wire
props.doc: the key, as wire index.

props.name: agent
props.doc: the agent bound or cleared.

props.name: bound
props.doc: 1 = bound, 0 = cleared.

events.doc: what the board daemon costs on its mac (docs/board.md, budgets: a 4 mib physical footprint, 0.1% of a core plugged in and idle, nothing measurable with no board). hourly while a board is plugged in, plus one row at each plug covering the time the board was away, so the no-board cost is measured without a timer running while idle.

props.name: footprintKib
props.doc: physical footprint at the sample, kib (vmmap): the process's own memory, what activity monitor shows. the budget's figure.

props.name: rssKib
props.doc: resident size at the sample, kib (ps rss). counts the shared CoreFoundation pages every IOKit client maps, so it reads about 5.4 mib above the process's own cost.

props.name: cpu
props.doc: percent of one core used since the last sample.

props.name: spanMs
props.doc: the wall time the cpu figure covers.

props.name: board
props.doc: 1 = the span had a board plugged in, 0 = the span ends at a plug.
